subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should OpenClaw expose agent-scoped durable keyed storage to external plugins, and if so should it extend `api.runtime.state.openKeyedStore` rather than introduce a parallel `context.cache` API?
rationale: Current surfaces cover global plugin state and session-owned state, but choosing a new external agent-scoped contract determines API ownership, trust policy, database access, lifecycle cleanup, and long-term compatibility.

options.title: Extend the keyed store
options.body: Add an explicit agent-scoped binding to the existing keyed-store API with host validation, quotas, cleanup semantics, and one real plugin integration as proof.

options.title: Keep current scopes
options.body: Retain global keyed storage for trusted plugins and direct plugins to session extensions, next-turn injections, or task flows for narrower state lifecycles.

options.title: Require a concrete use case
options.body: Pause API design until an affected external plugin supplies its current state model, failure mode, and why existing contracts cannot represent it.

recommendation.title: Extend the keyed store
recommendation.body: Add an explicit agent-scoped binding to the existing keyed-store API with host validation, quotas, cleanup semantics, and one real plugin integration as proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the closest existing SQLite-backed plugin state contract and is best positioned to assess whether it should gain an agent scope.
